title: Three-Paths Focus Slate — Q4 Staffing & OKR Draft
content:
Purpose

This doc is a lightweight, cross-functional draft for Q4 planning framed as three distinct resource/priority paths. It combines a compact OKR sketch, an exec update narrative, and a short all-hands agenda to align communications. The goal is to get rough alignment on which path we run with by week 2 of the planning cycle (decision checkpoint).

Executive summary (one paragraph)

We propose three rival priority paths for Q4 to reconcile growth and reliability constraints: 1) Growth-at-scale — prioritize hosted API adoption and developer funnels (marketing + SDK work); 2) Platform Resilience — prioritize SLO/observability, Dedicated SLA roadmap, and private deployment hardening; 3) Cost/Unit Optimization — prioritize Optimize (batching, quantization, routing) and runtime cost improvements. Each path implies different hiring, budget, and rollout cadence. We need an exec decision to finalize headcount tradeoffs and commit ~60% of cross-org engineering bandwidth.

High-level differences (table summary, written out)

- Path A — Growth-at-scale
  - Key bet: product-led velocity (self-serve onboarding + integrations) moves net revenue faster than marginal infra cost increases.
  - OKR sketch: O1: Increase self-serve signups to paid MRR by 35% MoM; O2: Improve first-5-min time-to-first-success for new devs to <10m; O3: Add 3 major SDK integrations (Go, Java, .NET).
  - Staffing: +6 SDK/DevRel hires, +2 growth PMs, +1 infra SRE to support burst traffic.
  - Risks: cost per token rises, increased support load, potential SLO violations under peak traffic if not scoped.

- Path B — Platform Resilience
  - Key bet: enterprises convert faster with demonstrable SLOs, auditability, and predictable ded. capacity.
  - OKR sketch: O1: Achieve 99.95% Dedicated availability SLA across control plane; O2: Roll out private VPC onboarding with KMS integration to 5 pilot customers; O3: Reduce incident-to-detection mean time by 40% via tracing and alerts.
  - Staffing: +4 SRE/infra, +2 security/compliance engineers, +1 product manager for Dedicated/private.
  - Risks: slower topline expansion; longer sales cycles but higher ACV.

- Path C — Cost/Unit Optimization
  - Key bet: lowering unit cost through runtime and Optimize features unlocks margin and price competitiveness; target improvement yields sustainable LTV/CAC.
  - OKR sketch: O1: Reduce per-token GPU cost by 25% (quantization + kernel selection improvements); O2: Deliver automated batching recommendations to 80% of customers and show 15% avg cost reduction; O3: Publish 5 reproducible workloads with optimized configs.
  - Staffing: +5 applied-ML/inference engineers, +2 product engineers for Optimize, +1 pricing analyst.
  - Risks: long runway to measurable revenue impact; engineering-heavy with delayed customer-visible wins.

Decision criteria (what execs should weigh)

- Revenue velocity vs. gross margin improvement (modelled scenarios attached in linked spreadsheet).
- Customer segmentation: which path helps our top 20 pilot customers vs long tail self-serve?
- Hiring lead times: SDK hires vs specialized inference engineers take different calendars.
- Regulatory/compliance commitments (some opportunities require resilience work).

Draft OKR language (compact, to be refined)

- Objective (example for Path C): Deliver unit-economics improvement to make Redwood the lowest-cost inference option for latency-sensitive enterprise workloads.
  - Key Result 1: Reduce average hosted GPU tokens cost by 25% vs baseline (Q3 end).
  - Key Result 2: 80% of Tier-1 customers adopt Optimize recommendations within 6 weeks of release.
  - Key Result 3: Two customers migrate from competitor endpoints citing cost reduction as the reason.

Exec update narrative (1–2 slides worth)

Slide 1 — Context & ask: "We’re at an inflection: top-line growth vs platform guarantees. Decision: choose primary Q4 path and commit people/budget."
Slide 2 — The three paths (one-liners + one risk each).
Slide 3 — Resource map: headcount buckets and funding ask per path (high/med/low).
Slide 4 — Contingency plan: how we fallback (e.g., start Path A and embargo new enterprise pilots until Dedicated SLA reaches X).

All-hands micro-agenda (45 minutes)

- 0–5m — Opening (CEO, 2 min context + ask).
- 5–12m — Leadership panel: each path sponsor gives 2–3 minute position (why this path).
- 12–20m — Quick data snapshot: revenue/cost/usage trends (finance + growth).
- 20–30m — Breakouts sign-up (theme-aligned rooms: Growth, Platform, Optimize) — 10-minute deep dives, capture top-3 tradeoffs.
- 30–40m — Readout: each breakout 2 minutes.
- 40–45m — Close & next steps (decision timeline, where to give feedback).

Comms timeline (short)

- Week 0 (today): share this draft with execs and product leads.
- Week 1: refine and run 90-minute leadership workshop (decision support materials pre-read).
- Week 2: leadership decision checkpoint (commit headcount and high-level OKRs).
- Week 3: all-hands + comms to entire company; team-level planning kickoff in week 3–4.

Open questions / parking lot (notes to self and leads)

- Can we get an accurate cost model for cross-region Dedicated capacity vs hosted blended rates? (Finance: ask for sensitivity matrix).
- Growth metrics baseline: what is the true conversion delta from new SDKs? Need growth experiments playbook.
- Hiring timeline: what are realistic earliest start dates for senior inference engineers vs SDK leads? (Recruiting to confirm).
- Sales impact: if we prioritize Path C, do we need a parallel small team to handle inbound enterprise requests?

Quick risks & mitigations

- Risk: Overcommitment to a single path leads to missed enterprise deals or outrun infra stability.
  - Mitigation: Reserve a 15% engineering float for cross-path criticals; maintain fallback policy in engineering roadmap.
- Risk: Customer confusion across messaging.
  - Mitigation: Unified external narrative that we are "balancing velocity and reliability" — detail per-segment communications.

Action items (next 10 days) — owner initials in parens

- Finance: produce headcount + spend delta per path (Lena).
- Recruiting: feasibility of hiring plan + time-to-fill (Samir).
- Product: refine OKR language to measurable KRs and alignment with team-level goals (Arjun).
- Marketing/Docs: draft all-hands skeleton and one-page explainer for customers (Maya).
- SRE: run capacity stress quick-check for Path A traffic assumptions (Elena).

Appendix (short)

- Quick notes on signals to watch after decision: Customer churn, average token cost, incident count by severity, time-to-onboard enterprise customer.
- Related artifacts: linked OKR spreadsheet, pilot customer list, draft all-hands slide deck (links above).

Tone & style notes: keep this doc conversational; it’s a working artifact for leadership alignment. Expect lots of inline edits. If you leave comments, tag with context and estimation of impact (high/med/low).

---

Draft log & provenance

End of draft
